Resolves #21181

The value-banding example now opens on 100 fictional colleagues, sorted into unequal country runs. Country banding starts on; Department banding adds a second level, independently of alternating row stripes. The grid fills its stage, controls stack above it on phones, and the explanation and catalog copy describe banding. The shared ConfigurationViewport and engine banding logic are unchanged.

Evidence: L3 (live browser checks, before/after captures, and the recorded catalog-cover producer) → L3 required. Requesting the ticket's design-seat review before code review; independent design approval and cover publication are not claimed.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/grid/ValueBandingExample.spec.mjs` verifies repeatable, nonempty staff records without the old placeholder names. Screenshots below show the rendered directory. |
| AC-2 | Outside CI: at 1440 × 900, the grid occupies 1058 × 860 px within its padded stage. The first country runs contain 4 Canadian, 7 Danish and 10 Finnish colleagues; all three are visible. The owning unit spec checks those run lengths. |
| AC-3 | Outside CI: Department banding adds and removes band classes on department cells. Tab from the theme button reaches row stripes, then Department banding; Space toggles the latter. CI-covered: the owning spec checks that department bands preserve country bands and row order. |
| AC-4 | The explanation and catalog record use banding terminology; neither describes the feature as grouping. |
| AC-5 | Outside CI: 390 × 844 and 1440 × 900, light and dark themes, each with Department banding off and on. Narrow layouts keep controls above the grid and allow horizontal scrolling for the remaining columns. |
| AC-6 | Before/after screenshots appear below for both requested sizes, including one and two band levels. Design-seat review is requested before code review and remains pending. |
| AC-7 | The official producer re-shot the default state: 1280 × 720 JPEG, 91,181 bytes, SHA-256 `1288d372083e6006a17bde7c650a56a3866c2e72e2bd96e3cda58082a4ab6360`. The updated recipe waits for the first country boundary without changing the default state. Cover and capture report are attached below. Publication destination: `neomjs/pages:resources_pub/website/examples/devmode/grid-value-banding-14.jpg`. |

## Design read (AC-6) — `a4e122a0b2`

**Verdict first: BETTER.** The released frame shows eleven rows of France in a 400 px box: no band boundary is visible, the names read `First_32`, and nothing says what the tint means. The new frame fills the stage, shows three country bands of different length on first sight, and its first sentence says what a band is.

I read this as the design seat Euclid routed here while the design owner is unavailable. I didn't build or write any of it. Instrument: I rendered the exact head and dev headless at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844, in both themes, with Department banding off and on, and measured the DOM. The images in the PR body are not the evidence for this read.

**Cold look** (two readers without session context, unlabelled pair, swapped order). Each read the desktop and phone frames and graded "after five seconds, would you understand value banding and want it?":

| Reader | Released | This head | Better |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (released shown first) | 2 | 7 | this head |
| 2 (this head shown first) | 2 | 7 | this head |

Both readers named the same weakness of the new frame: in the light theme the band is "a faint blue tint", and with both switches off the second level is not on screen. The default of one level is what #21181 prescribes ("Switch Department on for a second level"), so it stays. The light tint is the theme's band token, which every grid shares, not this example's; I'm capturing it as a defect note rather than asking it of this PR.

| AC | Measured at this head | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · no placeholder | No `First_` / `Last_` text in any frame; names unique (the spec's check, green in CI) | ✓ |
| 2 · stage height, ≥ 3 unequal bands | Grid 1058 × 860 inside a 1098 × 900 stage (20 px padding). First frame: Canada 4, Denmark 7, Finland 10, France 5 visible | ✓ |
| 3 · Department switch changes the frame, the sentence matches | Department cells band `11212221122111` when on, none when off. Country bands and row order are unchanged either way. The sentence names both switches and what each does | ✓ |
| 4 · not called grouping | Neither the frame nor the catalog copy uses the word | ✓ |
| 5 · 390 × 844, both themes | The controls stack above the grid, with no horizontal page overflow. The header theme button switches both themes, and both band levels read in dark | ✓ |

**One fix before merge (design):** the two switches touch. "Alternate row stripes" spans 262–280 px and "Department banding" 280–298 px, a 0 px gap; on dev each had `style: {marginTop: '10px'}`, which this PR removes. Their labels are 16 px against the explanation's 14 px (12 px on the phone), so the pair reads as one heavy block under the text. Restoring the base's top margin is enough.

**Optional (phone):** at 390 × 844 the Colleague column spans 293–473 px in a grid that ends at 378 px, so the first frame cuts names mid-word ("Robin Benne") and Role sits entirely off-screen. Narrower Country and Department widths at phone width would show whole names. It works as is, since the grid scrolls; this is polish.

The code review follows separately.
